{{Quote|For over a thousand generations, the Jedi knights<!--decapitalization of "knights" is intentional, since the film's captions format it that way--> were the guardians of peace and justice in the old<!--decapitalization of "old" is intentional, since the film's captions format it that way--> Republic. Before the dark times, before the Empire.|Obi-Wan Kenobi, to Luke Skywalker|<ref name="Episode IV" />}}
A '''Jedi''', often called a Jedi Knight, was a devotee to the ways of the [[Jedi Order]], an ancient order of [[Jedi Knight|protectors]] united by their [[Force-sensitive|ability]] to harness the [[Force power|power]] of [[the Force]]. Adhering to a [[Jedi Code|doctrine]] that favored the [[light side of the Force]], the Jedi aspired to attain a state of inner tranquility through calmness and [[meditation]] while avoiding emotions affiliated with the [[dark side of the Force]], such as anger and hatred. Nevertheless, Jedi philosophy did not forbid a Jedi from acting in self-defense or in the defense of others, and they were colloquially known as '''Space Wizards''' to citizens of [[the galaxy]]. To that end, a Jedi's only possession was their [[lightsaber]], a symbol of their role as guardians of peace and justice.

Before the [[time]] of the [[Galactic Empire]], Jedi worked with the [[Galactic Republic]] with a commitment to freedom and [[democracy]]. The Jedi and the Republic's ideals brought them into [[Jedi-Sith War|conflict]] with an order of dark side wielders known as the [[Sith]], who sought power and dominion over [[the galaxy]]. Emerging victorious from their wars with the ancient Sith, the Jedi carried on in their duty as peacekeepers for over a [[millennium]] until the [[First Battle of Geonosis|advent]] of the [[Clone Wars]] [[22 BBY|twenty-two years]] before the [[Battle of Yavin]]. Faced with a pan-[[Galaxy|galactic]] civil war between the Republic and [[Confederacy of Independent Systems]], the Jedi adopted the mantle of [[Jedi General|generals]] and [[soldier]]s in the [[Grand Army of the Republic]]. After three [[Standard year|years]] of conflict, the Jedi discovered that the Sith had deceived them and engineered the war to restore them back to power. However, just before the Sith were defeated, the Jedi were betrayed by one of their own—the [[Chosen One]] [[Anakin Skywalker]], who had been seduced to the dark side and anointed [[Darth]] Vader by the [[Sith Lord]] [[Darth Sidious]]. Using the Jedi's own [[clone trooper]]s to initiate a [[Great Jedi Purge|systematic purge]] of the Jedi Order, the [[Lord]]s of the Sith all but [[Order 66|eradicated]] the Jedi in one fell swoop, reducing the order from thousands of Jedi Knights guarding the galaxy, to a handful of survivors cast into [[Exile (punishment)|exile]] across the galaxy.

The Sith ruled the galaxy through the Empire for a [[Imperial Era|generation]], but did not succeed in completely wiping out the Jedi Order. As a result, [[Ezra Bridger]] and [[Luke Skywalker]] were, in turn, [[Jedi training|trained]] as new Jedi by [[Jedi Knight]] [[Kanan Jarrus]] and [[Jedi Master]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]], respectively. Skywalker, the son of Vader, was also taught the ways of the Jedi by [[Grand Master]] [[Yoda]] and fought for the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]] during the [[Galactic Civil War]]. On his [[death]] bed, Yoda gave his final apprentice the mandate of passing on his lessons to a new generation of Jedi. [[Battle of Endor|Shortly afterward]], Skywalker succeeded in redeeming his [[Parent|father]], who sacrificed himself to save his son by killing his [[Sith Master]], [[Galactic Emperor|Emperor]] Sidious, thereby destroying the Sith and fulfilling the prophecy of the Chosen One.

During the [[New Republic era|era]] of the [[New Republic]], Skywalker worked to rebuild the Jedi Order by training a dozen apprentices, including his young but powerful nephew, [[Ben Solo]], but Solo fell to the dark side and became Kylo Ren, apprentice of [[Supreme Leader]] [[Snoke]], [[Ren|master]] of the [[Knights of Ren]], and a [[warlord]] of the [[First Order]], while [[Jedi Temple of Luke Skywalker|Skywalker's training temple]] and students were [[Destruction of the Jedi Temple|destroyed]]. As the First Order [[First Order-Resistance War|rose to power]], Ren and Snoke sought to destroy Skywalker, who, in self-exile, briefly trained [[Rey Skywalker|Rey]] in the ways of the Jedi until he sacrificed himself to save the [[Resistance]], after which time Skywalker's sister, [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa]], continued her training. When a [[Cloning|reborn]] Darth Sidious—Rey's grandfather—[[Exegol broadcast|revealed]] himself to the galaxy, Ben Solo, the opposite in a [[Force dyad|dyad in the Force]] with Rey, was redeemed, and Rey sacrificed herself to [[Battle of Exegol|destroy]] the phantom Sith Lord, preventing the rebirth of the Sith Order. Rey was saved from death by Solo, who gave his life for hers, allowing the Jedi to live on.

==Description==
===Philosophy===
{{Quote|In order to master the ways of the Force, Jedi must forgo all attachment.|[[The Armorer]]|<ref name="Boba Chapter 5">{{BOBF|Chapter 5: Return of the Mandalorian}}</ref>}}
[[File:JediSitsAlone-InnerJedi.png|thumb|left|250px|To be a Jedi was to live a life of selflessness and devotion to the light side of the Force.]]
The [[Jedi Knight]]s focused on calmness and peace to channel their [[Force power|powers]] in [[the Force]], using the [[light side of the Force]] to serve in the capacity of guardians of peace and justice in [[the galaxy]].<ref name="Episode IV" /> Even so, the Jedi sought to preserve balance in the Force; the ancient prophecy of the [[Chosen One]] foretold of a being who would restore balance to the Force by destroying the [[Sith]]. In combat, whereas an enemy may grow impatient and rely on their overwhelming strength, a Jedi would [[Meditation|meditate]] and find serenity in their [[Brain|mind]] to focus.<ref name="Episode I" /> A Jedi used the Force for defense and knowledge rather than use it to gain power over others.<ref name="Episode V" /> Their chosen weapon the [[lightsaber]], a weapon with limitations, likewise symbolized the care a Jedi took wielding their gifts and that when a Jedi fights it is with intention and precision, ending conflict while injuring no more, or taking no more life, than the lightsaber's wielder chooses. <ref>{{StoryCite|story=The Lesson (Obi-Wan & Anakin)|book=Star Wars (2020) 25|sformatted=The Lesson (Obi-Wan & Anakin)}}</ref> Always supposed to put the needs of others before their own,<ref name="Path of Ven">''[[The High Republic: Path of Vengeance]]''</ref> a Jedi was supposed to be selfless<ref name="Episode III" /> and work to save others above themselves.<ref name="Light of the Jedi">''[[The High Republic: Light of the Jedi]]''</ref> Like all people, Jedi were imperfect and always needed to strive to better themselves, meaning it was impossible to be a "perfect Jedi."<ref name="Convergence">''[[The High Republic: Convergence]]''</ref>

Because of their ability in the Force, a Jedi, even if they lacked a physical weapon, was never defenseless,<ref name="Ahsoka novel">[[Ahsoka (novel)|''Ahsoka'']]</ref> and some Jedi were capable of appearing after [[death]] as [[Force spirit]]s.<ref name="Episode V" /><ref name="Episode VII">{{Film|VII}}</ref><ref name="Episode VIII" /> The Jedi considered themselves instruments of the Force,<ref name="Episode IV" /> and during the [[time]] of the [[Galactic Republic]], peacekeepers instead of [[soldier]]s.<ref name="Episode II" /> Striving to be majestic yet simple,<ref name="Light of the Jedi" /> knowledge, the Force, and self-discipline were considered the three pillars of Jedi strength.<ref name="Complete Visual New">''[[Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary, New Edition]]''</ref> Instead of acting for selfish aims,<ref name="Episode III" /> such as securing wealth or power, the Jedi focused their pursuits on learning, reaching enlightenment,<ref name="Path of Ven" /> helping others<ref name="Episode III" /> in a just fashion,<ref name="Convergence" /> and finding balance.<ref name="Age Qui-Gon">[[Age of Republic - Qui-Gon Jinn 1|''Age of Republic - Qui-Gon Jinn'' 1]]</ref> The Jedi believed that—no matter one's physical appearance—everyone was internally made up of light. Individuals who did not understand the Force took to calling Jedi "space wizards."<ref name="Light of the Jedi" />

Through the [[Jedi Order]] all Jedi belonged to, a Jedi was connected to the entire [[galaxy]].<ref name="Convergence" /> As part of the Order, a single Jedi had the advantage of a structured community to rely on and gain confidence from.<ref name="Light of the Jedi" /> In the opinion of [[Padawan]] [[Matthea Cathley]], the Jedi were better as a group than on their own.<ref name="Path of Ven" /> Similarly, Jedi Knight [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]] thought of the Order as something that proved that, in being a Jedi, he was part of something bigger than himself.<ref name="Obi-Wan and Anakin 5">[[Obi-Wan and Anakin 5|''Obi-Wan and Anakin'' 5]]</ref> Indeed, the Jedi could rely on their Order in tough times, enabling an individual Jedi to act in a bold fashion and make large scale choices about spreading light. One enemy of the Jedi, [[Eye of the Nihil]] [[Marchion Ro]], thus regarded the Jedi Order as something the Jedi would tap into, much like their ability to tap into the Force itself.<ref name="Light of the Jedi" />

The life of a Jedi was full of hardships. [[Jedi training|Training]] to become a Jedi was difficult, according to [[Jedi Master]] [[Qui-Gon Jinn]], and those who succeeded were faced with a hard life ahead.<ref name="Episode I" /> Adherence to the Jedi way required a disciplined mind and a strong sense of commitment, and it was considered unbecoming of a Jedi to seek adventure or excitement.<ref name="Episode V" /> The [[Jedi Code]] therefore regulated the lives of individual Jedi, their actions and beliefs, and the policies of the Jedi Order. While the Code permitted compassion, attachment and possession were forbidden to the Jedi.<ref name="Episode II" /> The Jedi believed that attachment led to jealousy, and greed in turn, and ultimately the fear of loss which was a pathway to the [[dark side of the Force]].<ref name="Episode III" /> Through the Force, the Jedi hoped to direct themselves through their passions, instead of acting in an impulsive manner.<ref name="Path of Deceit">''[[The High Republic: Path of Deceit]]''</ref> Forgoing attachment was also considered essential to a Jedi's progress in mastering their [[Force power]]s,<ref name="Boba Chapter 5" /> as their training could last from [[Standard year|years]] to a lifetime.<ref name="Boba Chapter 6">{{BOBF|Chapter 6: From the Desert Comes a Stranger}}</ref> Despite the importance of non-attachment in the Jedi vow, there was disagreement on what that specifically meant.<ref name="Midnight Horizon">''[[The High Republic: Midnight Horizon]]''</ref>

Some Jedi took it to mean they needed to suppress their emotions, such as vanquishing love and discomfort from themselves, whereas others believed trying to master emotion went against the ideals of the Order. For the latter group of Jedi, emotions like love were centered upon the idea of letting go. Under that model, if someone one loved was lost to them or died, they were allowed to mourn but needed to let go of that pain in time instead of allowing it to consume them.<ref name="Midnight Horizon" /> Indeed, the Jedi accepted death as a part of the natural course of life, believing that the deceased should be celebrated instead of mourned for becoming one with the Force.<ref name="Episode III" /> Detachment was nonetheless one of the most difficult lessons for Jedi to learn, as it took practice and repetition to master. Learning the lesson—that, to be a Jedi, one needed to "let go"—multiple times over his long life,<ref name="Midnight Horizon" /> [[Grand Master]] [[Yoda]] was able to carry the belief to his deathbed after a lifespan of nine [[Standard century|centuries]], even accepting his death—the death of all life—as the way of the Force.<ref name="Episode VI">{{Film|VI}}</ref>

Indeed, the Jedi understood feelings like love to be natural; Jedi were allowed to feel these emotions,<ref name="The Rise of Clovis">{{TCW|The Rise of Clovis}}</ref> but their task was to balance their strong feelings.<ref name="Midnight Horizon" /> With an understanding of their strongest emotions, it was hoped a Jedi would analyze what, deep down, made them feel the way they did. Able to then address their underlining motivations, the Jedi could formulate the best possible path forward instead of allowing themself to act without thinking. Attachments like romance were understood to be distractions from the Jedi mission of spreading justice and the light side: it represented a person tying themself down to one attachment, rather than opening themself up to the galaxy as a whole. Bound only to the Force and the Jedi Temple, relationships to a Jedi needed to be carefully handled in the name of their service to the Force.<ref name="Path of Deceit" /> Close friendships still existed and were valued,<ref name="Episode III" /> but a Jedi needed to understand their friends could be lost and need to be let go of at any given time.<ref name="Midnight Horizon" />

===Galactic sentiments===
{{Main|Anti-Jedi sentiment}}
{{Quote|People made holodramas about them, wrote stories. The Jedi were…''celebrities'', and rightly so.|[[The Archivist]]|<ref name="Crimson Reign 3">[[Crimson Reign 3|''Crimson Reign'' 3]]</ref>}}
[[File:Dont_Believe_the_Lies.png|thumb|right|250px|Throughout galactic history, anti-Jedi sentiment appeared amongst certain groups.]]
Throughout the [[Timeline of galactic history|history of the galaxy]], Jedi were often seen as a noble order that protected the galaxy and the [[Galaxy|Galactic]] Republic as the guardians of peace and justice.<ref name="DB:Order">{{Databank|jedi-order|Jedi Order}}</ref> In some cases, like [[Onderonian]]s, having the backing of a Jedi inspired confidence.<ref name="The Soft War Episode Guide">{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/the-soft-war-episode-guide|text="The Soft War" Episode Guide | The Clone Wars}}</ref> The skills associated with a Jedi Knight were revered and as such, their warrior prowess was known and respected to varies degrees from warrior-like cultures such as [[Mandalorian]]s.<ref name="A Friend in Need">{{TCW|A Friend in Need}}</ref> Some outsiders had exaggerated views of the sheer power an average Jedi possessed and attributed them with being able to do things the Jedi themselves considered more to be like divine action.<ref name="Light of the Jedi" />

However, [[anti-Jedi sentiment]] was also present throughout their history, stronger in some periods than others.<ref name="Crimson Reign 3" /> The Sith aimed to purge the galaxy of the Jedi and their ways.<ref name="DB:Order" /> Other groups and factions emerged with anti-Jedi sentiments; various [[Mandalorian]]s, like those of [[Death Watch]], held a grudge against the Jedi for their perceived crimes against [[Mandalore]] during the [[Mandalorian-Jedi War]].<ref name="A Friend in Need" /><ref name="Star Wars Rebels Showrunner Explains Major Knight of the Old Republic Reference">{{WebCite|url=http://comicbook.com/starwars/2017/02/18/star-wars-rebels-knights-of-the-old-republic-reference-confirmed|text=Star Wars Rebels Showrunner Explains Major Knight of the Old Republic Reference|author=Lucas Siegel|archivedate=20170220002112}}</ref> The [[Dagoyan Order]] also had a chilly relation with up until the later years of the Galactic Republic; early in its history, the Jedi Order had attempted to take in [[Bardottan]] [[Youngling|children]], causing them to cease most contact.<ref name="NoP" /> The [[E'roni]] spread stories of the Jedi, with some claiming the Jedi were miracle workers who used the power of levitation and "laser swords." Other E'roni, however, looked down on the Jedi as outsiders. Their rivals, the [[Eirami]], did not have stories of the Jedi but spoke of their "[[Krel (deity)|first god]]" in a similar way to how the Jedi described the Force.<ref name="Convergence" />

A cult known as the [[Path of the Open Hand]] believed the Jedi abused the Force by using it, and thus promoted anti-Jedi sentiment and the belief that the order was the reason for much of the galaxy's suffering. They rose to prominence on the planet [[Dalna]] during the early [[High Republic Era]],<ref name="Path of Deceit" /> during which time they began to spread their influence and beliefs across the [[Dalnan sector]]<ref name="Convergence" /> and the greater galaxy.<ref name="Path of Deceit" /> The Path declared that the Force did not belong to the Jedi, which was a claim the Jedi had never actually made.<ref name="Convergence" />

As the Jedi Order evolved and changed to face the challenges that were current to the galaxy, the way its members acted also had a habit of changing and evolving with time,<ref name="Star Wars (2020) 20">[[Star Wars (2020) 20|''Star Wars'' (2020) 20]]</ref> which often could have an impact on their relationship with the public.<ref name="Dangerous Debt">{{TCW|Dangerous Debt}}</ref> During the High Republic Era, the Jedi maintained the ideals of avoiding attachment<ref name="Midnight Horizon" /> but made sure to show great acts of compassion towards those who were suffering, such as offering hugs to those who were grieving.<ref name="THR 3">[[The High Republic (2021) 3|''The High Republic'' (2021) 3]]</ref> However, many Jedi active in the late Republic Era gave into their need to avoid attachments to a detrimental extent,<ref name="Episode III" /> resulting in them instead offering proclamations of the Force and the greater good to those who were grieving, which often left those who were suffering with bitterness and the feeling that the Force users did not truly care.<ref name="Dangerous Debt" />

When a Jedi Knight of the High Republic Era had acted in such a way to the young [[Axel Greylark]], as he was forced to leave his [[Lexxir Greylark|father]] behind so she could save him and the rest of a starship crew, it generated a lifelong hate for the Jedi in Greylark's heart. Rather than properly comfort the boy, the Jedi Knight had said his father's demise was the will of the Force before moving on with her duties. As he started to grow close to Jedi Knight [[Gella Nattai]], he explained the story to her. While she understood what the Jedi Knight had meant, she knew it would not help Greylark to repeat it and instead affirmed to him that caring for grieving children was important to the Jedi, despite the other Knight's poor word choice.<ref name="Convergence" /> As the Republic Era reached its end, however, the more distant approach won out,<ref name="Dangerous Debt" /> with many Jedi adopting a more detached persona<ref name="Episode III" /> that, unknowingly, created public dislike towards them.<ref name="Dangerous Debt" /> Whereas the Jedi of the High Republic did not believe qualities like the age someone came to the Order at or their [[midi-chlorian]] count to be determining factors in whether someone could be a Jedi,<ref name="What a Jedi Makes">{{StoryCite|story=What a Jedi Makes|book=Stories of Jedi and Sith}}</ref> the later Jedi did overwhelmingly value these factors.<ref name="Episode I" />

The High Republic Era also saw greater variance in Jedi lightsabers, with differing hilt designs and blade colors seeing greater use<ref name="THR 8">[[The High Republic (2021) 8|''The High Republic'' (2021) 8]]</ref> when compared to their late Republic counterparts.<ref name="Episode II" /> A shift in lightsaber design culture came during the High Republic Era's Nihil conflict, where the [[Guardian Protocols]]-minded Jedi Order gave the order to only create simple [[battle saber]] hilts: if there was to be great conflict, the Council reasoned that lightsabers would be lost and then replaced. As such, the Council ordered Jedi to only create the basic hilt design instead of more unique looks because basic battle sabers were faster to create and maintain in excess.<ref name="Shadows 1">[[The High Republic – Shadows of Starlight 1|''The High Republic – Shadows of Starlight'' 1]]</ref> The hilts of late Republic lightsaber were largely the same and basic in design,<ref name="Episode II" /> much like the lightsabers created under the battle saber order.<ref name="Shadows 1" /> All the same, the later period of the High Republic Era had continued to see variance in lightsaber color.<ref name="Trailer">{{SWYouTube|BtytYWhg2mc|The Acolyte | Official Trailer | Disney+}}</ref> The High Republic Jedi also acknowledged a Jedi needed to be more than their lightsaber,<ref name="Cataclysm">''[[The High Republic: Cataclysm]]''</ref> whereas the late Republic Jedi declared a lightsaber was "[their] life."<ref name="Episode II" />

Jedi of the High Republic Era each developed their own understanding of the Force and how to understand it,<ref name="Light of the Jedi" /> with Jedi being allowed to take on the position of "[[Wayseeker]]" to avoid the orders of the High Council and follow only the will of the Force. One [[Unidentified Wayseeker|Wayseeker]] went as far to become an [[Alderaanian]] singing sensation.<ref name="Into the Dark">''[[The High Republic: Into the Dark]]''</ref> Beyond establishing temples across the galaxy and working those temples into each planet's culture and environment,<ref name="Light of the Jedi" /> Jedi of the High Republic Era also made a true effort to live amongst the cultures they tried to protect. Instead of simply living in their temples most of the time<ref name="Yoda interview">{{SW|url=news/swca-2022-marvel-yoda-interview|text=SWCA 2022: Marvel's ''Star Wars: Yoda'' Miniseries Revealed}}</ref> and only leaving when a mission called,<ref name="Episode II" /> the Jedi of the High Republic called the galaxy overall their home,<ref name="Convergence" /> establishing new temples<ref name="Light of the Jedi" /> and new missions across the galaxy as they traveled to meet and help the galaxy's cultures.<ref name="Convergence" />

==History==
===Guardians of the Republic===
{{Quote|What was once a simple religious sect devoted to the light side of the Force evolved into the most influential group of peacekeepers in the history of the galaxy.|Luke Skywalker, on the Jedi Order|<ref name="Secrets of the Jedi">''[[Star Wars: The Secrets of the Jedi]]''</ref>}}
[[File:First_Jedi_Temple_TLJ.png|thumb|left|250px|The first Jedi Temple was located on Ahch-To, a distant planet in the Unknown Regions of the galaxy.]]
The Jedi were an order of ancient origins, having been present in the galaxy for over [[Millennium|one thousand]] generations.<ref name="Episode IV" /> Originally established at the [[first Jedi Temple]] on [[Ahch-To]] by the [[Prime Jedi]],<ref name="TLJ VD" /> the Jedi Order built [[Jedi temple|temples]] and outposts on numerous worlds throughout the galaxy, including [[Coruscant]], [[Ossus]], [[Tython]], and [[Jedha]]. The Jedi eventually came to align with the [[Democracy|democratic]] Galactic Republic and owed their allegiance to the [[Galactic Senate]].<ref name="Episode III" /> For a time, the Jedi were addressed using the honorary title of "[[Lord Jedi]]," but the title fell out of use in the millennium before the High Republic Era, with only the [[Togruta]]s keeping use of the title.<ref name="The Rising Storm">''[[The High Republic: The Rising Storm]]''</ref>

===Wars of the Old Republic===
{{Quote|There have not been battles like these since the days of the Old Republic.|Saesee Tiin|<ref name="Citadel Rescue">{{TCW|Citadel Rescue}}</ref>}}
[[File:JediVsSith-SOTS.png|thumb|right|220px|The Sith splintered from the Jedi to follow the dark side, spawning a rivalry that lasted for millennia.]]
When a [[Unidentified rogue Jedi|rogue Jedi]] was [[Exile (punishment)|exiled]] from the order after advocating the use of the dark side of the Force, they gained followers which led to the creation of the Sith<ref name="Sith">{{SWE|groups|sith|Sith}}</ref> during the [[Hundred-Year Darkness]].<ref name="Showdown on the Smuggler's Moon, Part II">[[Star Wars (2015) 9|''Star Wars'' (2015) 9]]</ref> The Jedi and Sith became bitter enemies,<ref name="Sacrifice">{{TCW|Sacrifice (episode)}}</ref> engaging in a number of battles and wars like the [[Sith war (Old Republic)|Sith war]],<ref name="NoP" /> the [[Battle of Takodana (Jedi versus Sith)|Battle of Takodana]],<ref name="TVD">''[[Star Wars: The Force Awakens: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> the [[Great Hyperspace War]],<ref name="NoP" /> the [[Great Sith War]],<ref name="Light of the Jedi" /> the [[Great Scourge of Malachor]],<ref name="Twilight of the Apprentice">{{Rebels|Twilight of the Apprentice}}</ref> the [[resurgence of the Sith]],<ref name="KoF">''[[Knights of Fate]]''</ref> and [[Darth Momin's destruction of a city|the defeat]] of [[Darth Momin]].<ref name="Dark Lord 22">[[Darth Vader (2017) 22|''Darth Vader'' (2017) 22]]</ref>

Another splinter group of Jedi emerged, calling themselves the [[Ordu Aspectu]]. Some records suggested they had hoped to give [[immortality]] to everyone in the galaxy, yet others believed that they may have killed Jedi [[Padawan]]s to try to achieve their goals.<ref name="Doctor Aphra 2" /> The Ordu Aspectu and the "orthodox" Jedi<ref name="Doctor Aphra 5">[[Doctor Aphra (2016) 5|''Doctor Aphra'' (2016) 5]]</ref> came to fight against each other in the [[Entruvia Conflict]], which ended with a [[Jedi–Ordu Aspectu treaty|peace treaty]]. The treaty allowed the Ordu to continue their research into immortality, but gave the Jedi Order the right to inspect the research. The [[Attack on Garn|doom of the Ordu Aspectu]], however, would result in the destruction of the splinter order and the Jedi inspectors: the leader of the Aspectu—a man named [[Rur]]—was able to download his mind into a computer, creating the [[Eternal Rur]], which wiped out everyone present.<ref name="Doctor Aphra 6">[[Doctor Aphra (2016) 6|''Doctor Aphra'' (2016) 6]]</ref> At another point in the Jedi Order's history, in the aftermath of the [[Corsair Wars]], Jedi Master [[Oo'ob]] broke from doctrine to create the [[Farkiller]].<ref name="Aphra 33">[[Doctor Aphra (2016) 33|''Doctor Aphra'' (2016) 33]]</ref>

The [[Great Jedi Library]] on Ossus was destroyed at some point prior to the [[Clone Wars]].<ref name="CL" /> At some point before the construction of the [[Imperial Palace|Jedi Temple]] on the planet Coruscant, the Jedi [[Evacuation of Ossus|evacuated]] a few of the [[holobook]]s and artifacts from the lost Great Library which made it to the [[Jedi Archives]] on Coruscant.<ref name="NoP" /> At some point, the mosaic floor of the [[First Temple]] on Ossus was salvaged and transported to the Order's newer headquarters on Coruscant.<ref name="CL" /> In the quasi-historical [[Qel-Droma Epics]], Ossus was decimated during the [[Cron Supernova]]<ref name="NoP" /> around [[4,000 BBY|4000 BBY]],<ref name="Supernova Date">According to ''[[Nexus of Power]]'', the [[Qel-Droma Epics]] dates the destruction of Ossus to approximately 4000 [[Standard year|years]] before the [[Imperial Era]].</ref> when the [[Sith Lord]] [[Naga Sadow]] triggered [[star]]s in the [[Cron Cluster]] to become [[supernova]]e. The Jedi had little warning of the coming cataclysm and prioritized the artifacts from the [[Chamber of Antiquities]] of the Great Jedi Library. Despite the efforts, they only managed to save a fraction of the artifacts housed on the planet, which made it to the Jedi Temple on the planet Coruscant via nearby [[Exis Station]], leaving the Great Library in ruins.<ref name="NoP" />

Also during the reign of the Old Republic, the Mandalorians, the [[Mandalorian warrior|warrior people]] of the planet Mandalore, launched a number of wars, often coming into conflict with the Jedi.<ref name="The Mandalore Plot">{{TCW|The Mandalore Plot}}</ref> Battles between the Mandalorians and Jedi dated back to the time of the [[Mandalorian crusaders]].<ref name="Shades Trivia Gallery">{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/shades-of-reason-trivia-gallery|text="Shades of Reason" Trivia Gallery}}</ref> According to legend, [[Mandalore the Great]] led the Mandalorians against the Jedi in a number of battles.<ref name="Chapter 8">{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 8: Redemption}}</ref> Eventually, the Mandalorians developed [[Mandalorian armor|their distinctive armor]]<ref name="Chapter 1">{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 1: The Mandalorian}}</ref> in order to combat their [[Force-sensitive]] enemies.<ref name="Complete Visual New" />

[[File:Mandalore_mural.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The world of Mandalore was devastated in the conflict between the Mandalorians and the Jedi.]]
The war against the Mandalorians ended in a decisive Jedi victory.<ref name="Trials of the Darksaber">{{Rebels|Trials of the Darksaber}}</ref> In the process, the surface of Mandalore was devastated<ref name="Creating Mandalore">[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars The Complete Season Two|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' The Complete Season Two]] Featurette: "Creating Mandalore"</ref> during [[Annihilation|the final battle]] between Mandalorian [[warlord]]s<ref name="Mandalorian super commando">{{SWE|groups|mandalorian-super-commando|Mandalorian super commando}}</ref> and the Jedi Order.<ref name="Creating Mandalore" /> Also at some point, as recounted in legend, a Force-sensitive Mandalorian named [[Tarre Vizsla]] was inducted into the Jedi Order. His lightsaber, the [[Darksaber]], was stored in the Jedi Temple on Coruscant after his death until members of [[House Vizsla]] [[Sacking of the Jedi Temple|broke in and stole the blade]]<ref name="Trials of the Darksaber" /> during the [[fall of the Old Republic]]. The Darksaber went on to be used to cut down many Jedi<ref name="The Mandalore Plot" /> and unite the Mandalorian people as a symbol of leadership.<ref name="Trials of the Darksaber" />

The Old Republic crumbled as a result of the Jedi-Sith wars, but its remnants and the Jedi still waged the [[Jedi-Sith War|final war]] against the Sith.<ref name="SWP">''[[Star Wars Propaganda: A History of Persuasive Art in the Galaxy]]''</ref> Ultimately, the Sith's greed for power caused them to turn on each other, which helped the Jedi [[Defeat of the Sith|defeat and decimate]] the weakened Sith. However, one [[Sith Lord]], [[Darth Bane]], secretly survived the destruction and continued the Sith by creating the [[Rule of Two]]<ref name="Sacrifice" /> and initiating the [[Grand Plan|Great Plan]].<ref name="HC 2">{{HelmetCollectionCite|2|Databank A-Z}}</ref> The Jedi would discover and then think they destroyed Bane's rule,<ref name="SW 2020 20">[[Star Wars (2020) 20|''Star Wars'' (2020) 20]]</ref> but the Sith continued to survive in secret under the Rule of Two.<ref name="Episode I" />

===The Great Peace===
====Jedi of the Republic====
=====Across the galaxy=====
[[File:PaoloVillanelliTHR1Virgin.png|thumb|right|220px|The Jedi reached the pinnacle of their power and influence during the height of the Galactic Republic.]]
After the defeat and assumed destruction of the Sith, the Jedi Order enjoyed a political ascension and saw an increase in recruitment. During the so-called "[[Republic Era|Great Peace]]" enjoyed by the Galactic Republic,<ref name="Rise">''[[Rise of the Separatists]]''</ref> which had reinvented itself after the defeat of the Sith,<ref name="SWP" /> the Jedi maintained a reputation<ref name="VoT" /> and role of being peacekeepers despite their limited numbers.<ref name="Episode II" /> The Jedi took part in<ref name="2022 THR 1">[[The High Republic (2022) 1|''The High Republic'' (2022) 1]]</ref> the [[Republic-Togruta conflict]].<ref name="The Rising Storm" /> The [[High Republic Era]] in particular was the height of the Jedi Order's power,<ref name="Light dust jacket">''[[The High Republic: Light of the Jedi]]'' hardcover dust jacket write up</ref> being a time of greatly expanded Jedi activity throughout the galaxy that even allowed them to stretch out far from the [[Core Worlds]].<ref name="Kylo 2">[[The Rise of Kylo Ren 2|''The Rise of Kylo Ren'' 2]]</ref> During the era, the Jedi worked closely with the Republic.<ref name="Light of the Jedi" /> In the days of the [[Great Hyperspace Rush]], the Jedi worked with [[Outer Rim Exploration Team]]s sent out by Supreme Chancellors [[Orlen Mollo]] and [[Kyong Greylark]], who both hoped to unite the galaxy. Even Jedi who were not currently working with [[Republic Pathfinder]]s were expected to perform similar work, introducing themselves to and learning from local cultures, as well as looking for possible temple locations and Force-sensitive children. The Jedi hoped to prove themselves to the people of the [[Outer Rim Territories]] as defenders they could rely on.<ref name="Path of Deceit" />

However, the Republic and Jedi's expansion into the Outer Rim brought them into conflict with the Path of the Open Hand cult, which believed the Jedi were actively hurting the galaxy by using the Force. As part of their campaign to root out the supposed abusers of the Force, the Path unleashed<ref name="Path of Deceit" /> a [[Shrikarai|Nameless]]<ref name="Trail of Shadows 5">[[The High Republic: Trail of Shadows 5|''The High Republic: Trail of Shadows'' 5]]</ref> later known as the [[Great Leveler]], which feasted upon Force users.<ref name="The Rising Storm" /> Jedi [[Savina Besatrix Malagán|Sav Malagán]] fought alongside a pirate crew led by [[Maz Kanata]] during the [[Battle of Jedha]].<ref name="HRA 9">[[The High Republic Adventures (2021) 9|''The High Republic Adventures'' (2021) 9]]</ref> The defeat of the Path would come with the [[Night of Sorrow]], during which the Path unleashed a number of Nameless against the Jedi. After the battle, Yoda and Jedi Master [[Creighton Sun]] decided to cover up the existence of the Nameless until more could be learned about the mysterious threat, reasoning that details about the beings getting out would be a danger to the Order. However, the decision<ref name="Cataclysm" /> left later Jedi vulnerable to an enemy they were not prepared for.<ref name="Trail of Shadows 5" /> Victory over the Path was seen as proof of how well the Jedi-Republic partnership worked out for the galaxy.<ref name="Cataclysm" /> However, later in the High Republic Era, some Jedi, such as Master [[Cohmac Vitus]], came to question whether it was right for the Jedi to work so closely with the Republic. In particular, Vitus pointed to the Night of Sorrow as a tragic event that had come about due to a joint Republic-Jedi effort.<ref name="Out of the Shadows">''[[The High Republic: Out of the Shadows]]''</ref>

Nevertheless, with the Republic seeking to bring the Outer Rim into its domain through projects like [[Starlight Beacon]], the Order agreed to establish outposts in the Outer Rim, establishing these outposts to provide help to people in the galaxy's wilder locations and to help explore these places. Prior to the [[Dedication of the Starlight Beacon|dedication of Starlight]], these outposts and their three to seven Jedi occupants—operating separately from the Jedi Temple on Coruscant—became the only force for justice on the [[Galactic Frontier]].<ref name="Light of the Jedi" /> During the High Republic, the foremost Jedi Master of the era, [[Avar Kriss]],<ref name="Databank Avar">{{Databank|avar-kriss|Avar Kriss}}</ref> held a rare Force power amongst the Jedi; able to detect the natural [[Force-bond]]s among Force-sensitives, she could strengthen them into a [[Song of the Force|network]] of many Jedi. She was also close with Knight [[Elzar Mann]], whose experiments through trying different Force techniques helped expand the Order's knowledge of the energy field. Under the leadership of Kriss, Mann and her were among the hundred Jedi dispatched to the [[Hetzal system]] in response to the sudden [[Great Hyperspace Disaster]], which began when fragments of the transport ''[[Legacy Run]]'' began to fall upon the star system thanks to the machinations of the [[Eye of the Nihil]] [[Marchion Ro]], whose [[Ro family|family]] had a history with the Jedi:<ref name="Light of the Jedi" /> their ancestors, [[Yana Ro]] and [[Marda Ro]], had been part of the Path of the Open Hand.<ref name="Path of Deceit" /> The Ro family would later remember "the faithful" as waging war with the Jedi because of their differing belief systems, believing the Jedi were unable to fulfill "balance" and were leading the galaxy to death.<ref name="The Rising Storm" />

To Marchion himself, the Jedi were not merely dangerous because they could use the Force; he believed their united Order gave them a structure to rely on, confidence, and a willingness to make large scale decisions, all in the name of spreading their light. Faced with an enemy who were therefore bold and strong, Ro, while not afraid of the Jedi, understood they would be a serious threat to his goals, which involved wiping them out. With Kriss using her network to inform her fellow Force-sensitives that the fragments contained living beings, the Jedi led the [[Republic Defense Coalition]] to rescue the star system and those trapped aboard the starship remains before turning their combined attention towards a fragment containing liquid [[Tibanna]]. Despite the failure of their first attempt and the loss of several Jedi, the Force users—joined in focus by Jedi in other locations in the galaxy—ultimately ensured the fragment did not collide with an [[R-class]] [[Star|sun]], saving the system. Additionally, the effort was broadcasted to various other worlds; only those who hated the Jedi were angered by their success.<ref name="Light of the Jedi" />

=====Conflict with the Nihil=====
[[File:THR-TheFallenStar-OOP-FullArt.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The peace of the Republic, maintained by the Jedi, was disrupted by the Emergences and the Nihil conflict.]]
As the galaxy was faced with the [[Emergences]], forcing the Republic to [[blockade]] a growing number of [[hyperspace route]]s into the Outer Rim, the Jedi Council believed the Jedi were going to be heavily needed in the region. Additionally, [[Nihil]] became known, leading to [[Nihil conflict|conflict between the pirates and the Jedi]]. Jedi Master [[Loden Greatstorm]] was captured by the Nihil during the [[raid on Elphrona]], playing into Ro's plans.<ref name="Light of the Jedi" /> During the Nihil conflict, the Republic began to push the Jedi to more closely work alongside them, with [[Supreme Chancellor]] [[Lina Soh]] and her [[aide]]s moving to insert themselves into the Jedi Council's affairs.<ref name="Out of the Shadows" /> Torturing Greatstorm for a year, Ro also came to collect all pieces to a [[Nameless control rods|family artifact]] he could use to unleash the Great Leveler. After the [[Valo Atrocity|massive Nihil raid]] on the [[Valo Republic Fair]], the Jedi tracked the Nihil to the planet [[Grizal]], only for Ro to unleash the Leveler during the [[Battle of Grizal|enusing battle]]; Greatstorm was killed, with his body left to turn to stone that soon crumbled, [[Padawan]] [[Bell Zettifar]] and Jedi Master Elzar Mann were left in states of shock, and Council member [[Stellan Gios]] was left to feel afraid.<ref name="The Rising Storm" />

Ro struck a further blow to the Jedi and Republic with the [[destruction of Starlight Beacon]], during which he deployed more Nameless. Unable to fight the creatures, the Jedi Order recalled all its members to Coruscant to strategize, only for Ro to [[Deployment of the stormseeds|claim]] a portion of the Outer Rim as [[Occlusion Zone|Nihil space]].<ref name="Eye 2">[[The High Republic: Eye of the Storm 2|''The High Republic: Eye of the Storm'' 2]]</ref> Eventually, the Nihil were destroyed.<ref name="SW7">[[Star Wars (2020) 7|''Star Wars'' (2020) 7]]</ref>

=====Continued "Great Peace" era=====
{{Quote|I remember a time when Jedi were not generals, but peacekeepers.|Satine Kryze|audio=NotGeneralsButPeacekeepers.flac|<ref name="VoT">{{TCW|Voyage of Temptation}}</ref>}}
As time went by, the Jedi continued to be involved in a number of the conflicts that [[sector]]s and [[planet]]s faced throughout the so-called "Great Peace." Though these conflicts could at times force them to act as military officers,<ref name="Rise" /> the Jedi did not view themselves as soldiers.<ref name="Episode II" /> The Jedi would also work as warriors, troubleshooters, and [[diplomat]]s for the Republic but claimed to be impartial judges. However, given that they were working for the Republic, trust in the Jedi was not the same for everyone. The citizens closer to the Core Worlds trusted them more than those in the Outer Rim Territories.<ref name="Rise" /> The Jedi became involved in conflicts like the [[Great Clan Wars|Mandalorian Civil War]],<ref name="VoT" /> the [[battle for Ontotho]],<ref name="Jedi 5">[[Jedi Fallen Order - Dark Temple 5|''Jedi Fallen Order - Dark Temple'' 5]]</ref> and the [[Stark Hyperspace War]].<ref name="Force Collection">{{ForceCollection|Saesee Tiin|star=4}}</ref>

====Return of the Sith====
{{Quote|Rage… it fuels us. But it won't be enough to stop the Jedi alone. They have numbers on their side. And the faith of the Republic.''"<br />"''For the moment. In time, and with careful planning, they will lose both.|Darth Maul and Darth Sidious|<ref name="Age Maul">[[Age of Republic - Darth Maul 1|''Age of Republic - Darth Maul'' 1]]</ref>}}
[[File:Malachor-AORDarthMaul1.png|thumb|right|250px|For generations the Sith plotted revenge on the Jedi for the defeat of their forebears.]]
Although the Jedi believed their sworn enemies to be extinct, the Sith had survived under the Rule of Two, influencing the galaxy from the shadows instead of battlefields. After around a thousand years of [[Sith Master]]s and [[Sith apprentice]]s,<ref name="Rise" /> the Sith Lord who held the rank of Master was [[Darth Sidious]],<ref name="Episode III" /> a [[Naboo (people)|Naboo]] who had been trained by the [[Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Darth Plagueis]].<ref name="USW">''[[Ultimate Star Wars]]''</ref> After betraying Plagueis by killing him in his sleep, Sidious sought to accomplish the Sith plan to bring the galaxy under his control as its [[Galactic Emperor]].<ref name="Episode III" /> Sidious also had his own Sith apprentice, [[Maul|Darth Maul]]. Due to his desire to kill Jedi, Maul killed Padawan [[Eldra Kaitis]] on the [[moon of Drazkel]], but her death did not satisfy his bloodlust.<ref name="Darth Maul 5">[[Darth Maul (2017) 5|''Darth Maul'' (2017) 5]]</ref> Thus, establishing a fake [[Kaitis Cartel|cartel]] under Kaitis's name, Maul continued his hunt and killed the Force-sensitive [[thief]] [[Zek Peiro]]. Not wanting the Jedi to learn of his plans, Sidious brought Maul to<ref name="Age Maul" /> the ancient Sith world<ref name="Twilight of the Apprentice" /> of [[Malachor]] to teach him about patience. Maul experienced a [[Force vision]] of a life where he was a Jedi before being surrounded by dozens of them, teaching him that their light side rivals had numbers and the respect of the Republic for the time being.<ref name="Age Maul" />

Sidious' public identity was Sheev Palpatine, the [[senator]] of his [[homeworld]] of [[Naboo]]. Living a double life allowed him to pursue political power in the Senate while conspiring to overthrow the Republic and its Jedi protectors as Sidious.<ref name="Secrets of the Sith">''[[Star Wars: The Secrets of the Sith]]''</ref> He planned to become [[Supreme Chancellor]] of the Republic to bring about his rule, so he ordered his pawns in the [[Trade Federation]] to [[Invasion of Naboo|blockade]] his own home planet<ref name="Episode I" /> to generate sympathy in the Senate<ref name="On the Front Lines">''[[Star Wars: On the Front Lines]]''</ref> and make Supreme Chancellor [[Finis Valorum]] look weak.<ref name="Sidious BioGal2">{{Databank|darth-sidious-biography-gallery|Darth Sidious Biography Gallery}} {{C|Image 2 caption}}</ref> When Valorum sent two [[ambassador]]s, Jedi Master Qui-Gon Jinn and Padawan [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]], to negotiate an end to the blockade, Sidious ordered them killed, but the two Jedi [[Escape from the Saak'ak|escaped]] to Naboo's surface and [[Capture of Theed|rescued]] [[Monarch of Naboo|Queen]] [[Padmé Amidala Naberrie|Padmé Amidala]] and her entourage.<ref name="Episode I" />

Due to the damage sustained during their escape, the [[Naboo Royal Starship]] needed to land on the [[desert]] planet of [[Tatooine]]. On Tatooine, Jinn met Anakin Skywalker, a young Force-sensitive human who he came to believe was the Chosen One. In fact, thanks to his power in the Force, Skywalker won the [[Boonta Eve Classic]], which won him freedom from his slavery under [[Watto]] the [[junk dealer]], albeit without freeing his mother, [[Shmi Skywalker Lars|Shmi]], and a new [[T-14 hyperdrive generator]] for the Royal Starship. Before leaving the planet, Jinn was suddenly [[Duel on Tatooine|attacked]] by Maul, who had been sent to Tatooine by Sidious. Jinn escaped, marking the first time a Jedi had contact with a Sith<ref name="Episode I" /> and survived to warn the Order<ref name="Darth Maul 5" /> in a thousand years.<ref name="Episode I" />

[[File:Jedi_Council_EP_I.jpg|thumb|left|250px|During the Invasion of Naboo, the Jedi learned of the Sith's survival and the existence of the Chosen One.]]
On the Republic capital of Coruscant, the [[Jedi High Council]] were disturbed by the potential return of the Sith and unwilling to begin Skywalker's training, citing his fear and believing it could lead to the dark side. They then dispatched Jinn and Kenobi back to Naboo when Amidala chose to return, as she had only managed to call for an [[Supreme Chancellor election, 32 BBY|election]] after being deceived by Palpatine, which would soon lead to Palpatine's victory. During the ensuing [[Battle of Naboo]], Jinn and Kenobi engaged Maul in yet another duel, while Skywalker, joined by [[astromech droid]] [[R2-D2]], joined the space battle against the [[Lucrehulk-class battleship|''Lucrehulk''-class Battleship]] ''[[Vuutun Palaa]]'' in a [[N-1 starfighter]]. Skywalker eventually crashed aboard the [[warship]] and, in an attempt to take out advancing [[OOM-series security droid]]s, fired two [[proton torpedo]]es that instead collided with a [[reactor]]. The ensuing explosion rippled throughout the [[battleship]], destroying the craft and therefore shutting down the entire [[Trade Federation Droid Army]] below.<ref name="Episode I" />

Elsewhere, Maul managed to kill Jinn while he was separated from Kenobi, though the Padawan then engaged Maul and cut the Sith Lord in half, ending the duel. In his dying breaths, Jinn asked Kenobi to train Skywalker, which the Jedi Council agreed to. Additionally, at the [[funeral of Qui-Gon Jinn]], Jedi Masters Yoda and [[Mace Windu]] spoke about the Sith, unsure whether it was the Sith Master or Sith apprentice who had been defeated.<ref name="Episode I" /> Kenobi was promoted to be a Jedi Knight with Skywalker as his Padawan.<ref name="Episode II" /> Though presumed dead, Maul had survived the duel. Sustained by his newfound hatred of Kenobi,<ref name="Revenge">{{TCW|Revenge (episode)}}</ref> he was left in exile on the garbage world of [[Lotho Minor]] for years to come.<ref name="Brothers">{{TCW|Brothers (episode)}}</ref>

===Fall of the Republic===
====The Clone Wars====
{{Quote|I am sure you are aware that the Jedi did not initiate the Clone Wars. Our only intention is to end it and restore peace to our galaxy.''"<br />"''What difference does it make who started the war, and who only wants to end it? No side is free of fault. It takes two to fight.''"<br />"''But isn't liberty worth fighting for?''"<br />"''But is it worth killing for? Fighting for something doesn't necessarily mean that you have to destroy everything in your path. Only when you lay your arms down and pursue a course of non-violence, can you make this claim to me that the Jedi are peacekeepers.|[[Aayla Secura]] and [[Tee Watt Kaa]]|<ref name="Jedi Crash">{{TCW|Jedi Crash}}</ref>}}
[[File:JediGeonosisArena.png|thumb|right|250px|The Jedi were too few in number to protect the Republic against an army of battle droids.]]
From [[24 BBY]]<ref name="24 BBY date">''[[Rise of the Separatists]]'' dates the [[Raxus Address|beginning]] of the [[Separatist Crisis]] to two [[Standard year|years]] before the [[Clone Wars]], which ''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates as beginning in [[22 BBY]]. Therefore, the Separatist Crisis must have begun in [[24 BBY]].</ref> to [[22 BBY]],<ref name="Timelines" /> the galaxy was faced with the [[Separatist Crisis]], a plot manufactured by the Sith. Several thousand [[star system]]s sought to secede to the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems]], a breakaway government led by its [[Head of State]], [[Dooku]], the latter of whom was following Sidious's command. The political tensions boiled into a full-scale war on [[Geonosis]], where the Separatist-aligned [[Geonosian]]s [[Death penalty|sentenced]] Kenobi, Skywalker, and the now-[[Senator]] Amidala to death. They were rescued by the arrival of a [[Jedi assault team]] led by Windu and then a force of [[clone trooper]]s, an army of [[Cloning|cloned]] soldiers recently discovered by Kenobi on the planet [[Kamino]], led by Yoda. In the subsequent actions of the [[First Battle of Geonosis|Battle of Geonosis]], the Jedi led the clones into battle against the [[Separatist Droid Army]], but Dooku managed to escape from Kenobi, Skywalker, and Yoda. Thus, the battle had served to launch the [[Clone Wars]], the first pan-galactic war<ref name="Episode II" /> since the alleged extinction of the Sith.<ref name="Rise" /> The start of the war shook the balance of the Force.<ref name="Battle of GeoTrailer">{{EASWYouTube|W-lwHrw_914|Star Wars Battlefront II: Battle of Geonosis Official Trailer|date=2018-11-21}}</ref> Dooku informed his master that the war had begun, which satisfied Sidious, who said everything was going as planned.<ref name="Episode III" />
[[File:Assault_on_Mandalorian_supply_outpost.png|left|thumb|250x250px|The Jedi served as generals of the Grand Army of the Republic throughout the Clone Wars.]]
There were ten thousand Jedi in the galaxy before the Clone Wars,<ref name="Path of the Jedi">{{Rebels|Path of the Jedi}}</ref> but many were killed during the conflict,<ref name="Assassin">{{TCW|Assassin (episode)}}</ref> with one Separatist leader, [[General]] [[Grievous]], even being a [[Jedi hunter]]<ref name="Databank Grievous">{{Databank|general-grievous|General Grievous}}</ref> who took the lightsabers of his victims as trophies.<ref name="Lair of Grievous">{{TCW|Lair of Grievous}}</ref> Another one of Dooku's agents was the [[Dark Acolyte]] [[Asajj Ventress]], who had been a Padawan to Jedi Knight [[Ky Narec]] in the years before the Clone Wars.<ref name="Nightsisters">{{TCW|Nightsisters (episode)}}</ref> During the war, Jedi Knights and Masters became the [[Jedi General]]s in the [[Grand Army of the Republic]], while their Padawans became lower ranking [[Jedi Commander]]s.<ref name="Clone Wars film">[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (film)|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' film]]</ref> The war against the Separatists was fought across the galaxy for three years,<ref name="Catalyst">''[[Catalyst: A Rogue One Novel]]''</ref> during which the Jedi inspired creative thinking and independence in the clones.<ref name="TCW|Fugitive">{{TCW|Fugitive}}</ref> Jedi like [[Plo Koon]],<ref name="Rising Malevolence">{{TCW|Rising Malevolence|Rising ''Malevolence''}}</ref> Kenobi,<ref name="Battle Tales 5">[[Star Wars Adventures: The Clone Wars – Battle Tales 5|''Star Wars Adventures: The Clone Wars – Battle Tales'' 5]]</ref> Yoda,<ref name="Ambush">{{TCW|Ambush}}</ref> and Skywalker respected the clones as individuals.<ref name="Darkness">{{TCW|Darkness on Umbara}}</ref>
[[File:Felucia-Skywalker.jpg|thumb|220x220px|Anakin Skywalker was considered the greatest warrior the Jedi had during the war, becoming known as the "Hero With No Fear".]]
By fighting the Clone Wars, the Jedi, particularly younger members of the Order, ran the risk of losing their way by focusing on power to win.<ref name="Lair of Grievous" /> Their new role as battlefield generals also made some people cast doubt on their role as "peacekeepers,"<ref name="VoT" /><ref name="Jedi Crash" /> with one Padawan, [[Barriss Offee]], and other Republic citizens even coming to view the Jedi to be responsible for the war. Falling to the dark side and thinking her Order had fallen from the light to be an army that only benefitted the dark side, Offee arranged for a [[bombing of the Jedi Temple hangar]] and framed her friend, fellow Padawan [[Ahsoka Tano]], to take the fall. One of the few people to stand with Tano was Skywalker, who was Tano's master and friend. He uncovered and exposed Offee as the true culprit during [[Trial of Ahsoka Tano|Tano's trial]]. Nevertheless, with her faith in the Order shaken, Tano left the Jedi to go on her own path,<ref name="The Wrong Jedi">{{TCW|The Wrong Jedi}}</ref> but she remained on the light side and acted, according to [[Rafa Martez]], in the way the Jedi should have been.<ref name="Together Again">{{TCW|Together Again}}</ref> Meanwhile, Skywalker greatly missed his Padawan<ref name="In Search of the Crystal">{{TCW|In Search of the Crystal}}</ref> and was frustrated with the Jedi Council, feeling they had betrayed his friend.<ref name="backstories">''[[Darth Vader: Sith Lord]]''</ref> During the war, Skywalker gained prominence and recognition for his victories on the battlefield, being considered the greatest warrior of the Jedi Order during the Clone Wars.<ref name="Shroud of Darkness" />

====The End of the Jedi====
{{Quote|The Jedi were ''good''. Like all of us, they failed to secure the peace. They were drawn into the war like everyone else, and their hands were ''not'' clean. If I can accept the blame for my part, they certainly earned their share, too. ''But'' for thousands of years they could have ruled the galaxy, and instead they chose to serve. They had their own vested interests, their own ways of politicking. But they believed their power came with an obligation to live humbly, to do good without asserting authority. Maybe they failed to live up to those ideals in the end. I haven't seen your evidence. What do ''I'' know about the extent of their betrayals? But they were good and they were ordinary and they were fallible, and even the most smug and arrogant were trying to hew to a tradition older than the Republic. They deserved better than to die at the hands of power-hungry old men who saw them as a threat. ''We'' deserved better than to lose another people, another religion, from the universe. All of us are poorer for their loss. ''[…]'' The Jedi deserve justice… or at least a decent funeral.|Mon Mothma, to Soujen Vak-Nhalis|<ref name="MoF">''[[Reign of the Empire: The Mask of Fear]]''</ref>}}
[[File:DuelonCoruscant.jpg|thumb|250px|Having learned that the Supreme Chancellor was a Sith Lord, the Jedi moved to arrest Darth Sidious before his plans came to fruition.|left]]
In the [[Battle of Coruscant]], which was staged by Sidious, in order to lure Anakin to the dark side and eventually make the young Jedi his apprentice, Dooku was betrayed by his master who had him killed by Skywalker. Following the battle, Skywalker had visions of Amidala, who he had [[Wedding of Anakin Skywalker and Padmé Amidala|secretly married]], dying in childbirth. Shortly thereafter, Palpatine, who had long since befriended Skywalker to manipulate him, informed the Jedi Knight that he was in fact Darth Sidious, the Sith Master behind the war and the target the Jedi had been searching for. After Skywalker informed Windu of Palpatine's identity and deception, the Jedi Master led [[Kit Fisto]], [[Agen Kolar]], and [[Saesee Tiin]] to [[Duel in Palpatine's office|arrest the Supreme Chancellor]]. The mission ended in failure, with Sidious cutting down all but Windu, and Skywalker himself arriving just as Windu gained the upper hand on Sidious. Believing that the Sith possessed the power to save Amidala, Skywalker betrayed Windu by helping Sidious take him out, before betraying the Jedi as a whole and kneeling before the Sith Master. Thus, Sidious had used Skywalker's anger with the Council and fear of losing Amidala to turn him to the dark side of the Force, making the Jedi's own Chosen One into his new Sith apprentice, Darth Vader.<ref name="Episode III" />

[[File:Grogus_Flashback.png|thumb|250px|Through Order 66, the Sith initiated a galaxy-wide purge that rendered the Jedi virtually extinct.]]
To launch the [[Great Jedi Purge]], Sidious ordered the clone troopers across the galaxy to execute [[Order 66]],<ref name="Episode III" /> which branded the Jedi and any clone who tried to help them as traitors who needed to be executed. Many of the clone troopers had befriended their Jedi leadership, but their loyalty was forcibly erased due to their biochips, which Sidious and Dooku had implanted in the clones during their youth. With Sidious issuing the order, this activated the clones' biochips, which brainwashed them into believing that the Jedi were traitors to the Republic, leading to them turning on their Jedi commanders.<ref name="Shattered">{{TCW|Shattered}}</ref> Jedi across the galaxy were therefore betrayed and gunned down by their own soldiers. Additionally, Vader [[Operation: Knightfall|led]]<ref name="Episode III" /> his elite<ref name="Battlefront II">''[[Star Wars Battlefront II]]''</ref> [[501st Legion]] into the Jedi Temple itself, murdering everyone, even the younglings, they found inside.<ref name="Episode III" /> Though Order 66 only explicitly targeted the Jedi, other Force-sensitives would find themselves in its crosshairs; Maul and Tano were both targeted aboard the [[Venator-class Star Destroyer|''Venator''-class Star Destroyer]] ''[[Tribunal]]'' by the [[332nd Division]], though Maul escaped aboard a [[Nu-class attack/transport shuttle|''Nu''-class transport]], while Tano and [[Clone Captain]] [[Rex|CT-7567]] "Rex," whose control chip had been removed by the former Padawan, fled aboard a [[BTL-B Y-wing starfighter/bomber]] as the ''Tribunal'' crashed.<ref name="Victory and Death">{{TCW|Victory and Death}}</ref>

As Vader cut down the [[Executive Separatist Council|Separatist Council]] on the volcanic world of [[Mustafar]], as per the command of Sidious, who betrayed and orchestrated the Council's death, Sidious used Windu's strike against him as an excuse to brand the Jedi as traitors before vowing to hunt down the surviving members of the Order and [[Proclamation of the New Order|transforming the Republic]] into his [[Galactic Empire]]. Yoda tried to rescue the galaxy from the new Sith Emperor, but he was not able to kill Sidious, and went into exile. When Amidala confronted her husband on Mustafar, he was enraged to see Kenobi, who had secretly stowed away aboard her [[J-type Naboo star skiff]]. After encasing Amidala in a [[Force choke]], Kenobi and Vader engaged in a [[Duel on Mustafar|lightsaber duel]], which ended when Kenobi left Vader to die near a lava river. A short time later, Amidala died in childbirth, with her two children, [[Luke Skywalker|Luke]] and [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia]], separated to keep them safe. Leia was taken to live with the [[House of Organa]] on [[Alderaan]], while Luke was taken to Tatooine to live with his aunt and uncle, [[Beru Whitesun Lars|Beru]] and [[Owen Lars]], while being watched over by Kenobi. Meanwhile, Vader had survived as well and was given a [[Darth Vader's armor|suit of life support armor]] to survive.<ref name="Episode III" /> Immediately after his reconstruction, Sidious tasked Vader with taking a [[kyber crystal]] from a Jedi to [[Bleeding|bleed]] it to be his own.<ref name="Dark Lord 1">[[Darth Vader (2017) 1|''Darth Vader'' (2017) 1]]</ref>

[[File:Darth_Vader_Dark_Lord_of_the_Sith_3_Textless.jpg|thumb|220px|The remaining Jedi were hunted by the Sith Lord Darth Vader, who was once the Jedi Knight Anakin Skywalker.|left]]
Needing to find a Jedi who had survived the purge, Vader used the database on the Jedi [[space station]] ''[[Brighthome]]'' to locate a Jedi who had taken the [[Barash Vow]], pointing him to Jedi Master [[Kirak Infil'a]]<ref name="Dark Lord 2">[[Darth Vader (2017) 2|''Darth Vader'' (2017) 2]]</ref> on the [[Mid Rim Territories|Mid Rim]] river [[moon]] of [[Al'doleem]]. After arriving,<ref name="Dark Lord 3">[[Darth Vader (2017) 3|''Darth Vader'' (2017) 3]]</ref> Vader and Infil'a [[Mission to Al'doleem|began a duel]] that ended with the Sith Lord killing the Jedi Master and flooding the [[Am'balaar City|city]] below. Vader also successfully stole [[Kirak Infil'a's lightsaber|his lightsaber]] for its kyber crystal.<ref name="Dark Lord 4">[[Darth Vader (2017) 4|''Darth Vader'' (2017) 4]]</ref> Thus, as Sidious ordered, Vader went to Mustafar to bleed the crystal to his will. Though it presented the Sith Lord with a vision where he returned to the light side of the Force, Vader rejected this and twisted the crystal to the dark side.<ref name="Dark Lord 5">[[Darth Vader (2017) 5|''Darth Vader'' (2017) 5]]</ref> Meanwhile, word spread throughout the galaxy's population that the Jedi had apparently betrayed the Republic and that their Order had been destroyed for it.<ref name="K2">[[Kanan 2|''Kanan'' 2]]</ref> Organa launched an [[investigation into the framing of the Jedi]] on the belief that, if he could prove Palpatine's evidence against the Jedi was fabricated, the Imperial project would collapse and justice would be served to the Jedi. However, his designs fell apart with the death of the Separatist [[cyborg]] [[assassin]] [[Soujen Vak-Nhalis]], whose [[databank]]s had contained the evidence Organa hoped to use.<ref name="MoF" />

===The Jedi Purge===
{{Quote|We seek a dangerous fugitive. This is no common anarchist but a devotee of the treasonous Jedi Order. Failure to turn over this traitor will result in a charge of sedition. Turn yourself in or everyone present shall face summary execution.|[[Second Sister]]|<ref name="JFO" />}}
The Empire's official explanation for the end of the Clone Wars<ref name="Catalyst" /> correctly stated that<ref name="Episode III" /> the Jedi had been killed in massive numbers, with the Empire stating it was by the thousands, that the Jedi Temple had been the site of a battle, and that the few survivors had fled throughout space. However, they also claimed the Force had dispersed. Though this explanation was not universally accepted, most people in the galaxy accepted the destruction of the Jedi, just as they had accepted the sacrifices of the clones, if it meant the war was over. To [[Lyra Erso]], it seemed as though mere [[Standard week|weeks]] passed before, without much grief or mourning, the Jedi Order had almost entirely been reduced to a myth.<ref name="Catalyst" /> In fact, many celebrated the destruction of the Jedi,<ref name="Dark Lord 1" /> having believed Sidious's claims of a Jedi rebellion<ref name="Episode III" /> and other Imperial propaganda<ref name="Dark Lord 1" /> that firmly squared the galaxy's recent troubles on the Order.<ref name="Launchpad229">{{InsiderCite|229|Launchpad}}</ref> Other citizens, meanwhile, simply blamed the Jedi for failing to prevent the Clone Wars or to more quickly end it.<ref name="MaskFear">''[[Reign of the Empire: The Mask of Fear]]''</ref>

Using fear, new laws, and its vast military, the Empire worked to crush surviving Jedi and their remaining supporters, creating such a fear about even discussing the Jedi that knowledge of them died off, as it was not passed down.<ref name="Crimson Reign 3" /> It was illegal to help Jedi during the Imperial Era; the [[parent]]s of [[Dak Ralter]] were given lifelong sentences for smuggling surviving Jedi Knights to safety.<ref name="Against All Odds">{{StoryCite|story=Against All Odds (From a Certain Point of View)|book=From a Certain Point of View: The Empire Strikes Back}}</ref> Due to the Empire's interest in eliminating the Jedi, rewards were offered to those who surrendered them.<ref name="JFO" /> Regardless of whether he was alive or dead, a Jedi could yield a high reward to a [[bounty hunter]].<ref>''[[Star Wars: Tales of the Underworld]]'' - "[[Friends]]"</ref> Surviving Jedi who tried to uphold the Order's ways became known as [[Jedi Arbiter]]s,<ref name="Disciples">''[[Disciples of Harmony]]''</ref> with those they trained out in the galaxy described as [[Bokken Jedi]] by the fallen Jedi [[Baylan Skoll]].<ref name="Part Six">{{Ahsoka|Part Six: Far, Far Away}}</ref> [[Vanzell Mar-Klar]] and their Padawan, [[Nedriss Narr]], tried to train a new generation of Knights in a hidden temple.<ref name="Trials">''[[Jedi Training: Trials of the Temple]]''</ref> However, other survivors were mentally beaten and decided to simply survive in the new era, rather than use their abilities for the common good.<ref name="JFO" />

[[File:OrderOfInquisitors-PromiseOfPower.png|thumb|250px|Inquisitors were fallen Jedi who hunted their former brethren as agents of the Sith and the Galactic Empire.]]
With Order 66 still in effect,<ref name="Star Wars 5">[[Star Wars (2020) 5|''Star Wars'' (2020) 5]]</ref> the Empire continued to hunt Jedi who had survived the protocol, with Sidious establishing the [[Inquisitorius]] to seek out and kill the survivors.<ref name="Dark Lord 6">[[Darth Vader (2017) 6|''Darth Vader'' (2017) 6]]</ref> The next survivor Vader [[Hunt for Jocasta Nu|encountered]] was former [[Chief Librarian]] [[Jocasta Nu]],<ref name="Dying Light II">[[Darth Vader (2017) 8|''Darth Vader'' (2017) 8]]</ref> who had recorded her knowledge in [[holocron]]s in a [[Jocasta Nu's cache|secret collection]] away from Imperial eyes. She returned to Coruscant to prevent the Empire from discovering a [[Kyber memory crystal]] list of Force-sensitive children,<ref name="Dying Light I">[[Darth Vader (2017) 7|''Darth Vader'' (2017) 7]]</ref> leading to her conflict with Vader and the Inquisitors. After her capture, she revealed the Emperor wanted her alive to access the list of children, whom he would turn into more dark side servants. Vader arranged for her death and destroyed the crystal, preventing such a future.<ref name="Dark Lord 10">[[Darth Vader (2017) 10|''Darth Vader'' (2017) 10]]</ref> Over the years, Vader and the Inquisitorius hunted down what remained of the Jedi Order.<ref name="Twilight of the Apprentice" /> Additionally, a Force-sensitive criminal named [[Kilmera Skale]], who allied with [[Imperial Security Bureau|ISB]] [[Special Agent]] [[Malor Phiatt]], pretended to be a Jedi to entrap those who survived the execution of Order 66.<ref name="EV">''[[Endless Vigil]]''</ref>

A year into the Empire's reign in [[18 BBY]],<ref name="18 BBY date">According to ''[[Ultimate Star Wars, New Edition]]'', the [[invasion of Mon Cala]] took place a year into the [[Darth Sidious|Emperor's]] rule. Since ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' dates the beginning of Imperial rule to [[19 BBY]], the occupation of Mon Cala took place in [[18 BBY]].</ref> the eighty-third [[King of Mon Cala]], [[Lee-Char]],<ref name="Prisoners">{{TCW|Prisoners}}</ref> was manipulated by [[Ferren Barr]],<ref name="Dark Lord 17">[[Darth Vader (2017) 17|''Darth Vader'' (2017) 17]]</ref> a surviving Padawan who had turned away from the path of the Jedi in order to destroy the Sith.<ref name="TSWB">''[[The Star Wars Book]]''</ref> Although he and the majority of his [[Ferren Barr's disciples|disciples]] were killed by Vader and his forces during the [[Invasion of Mon Cala|Imperial invasion of Mon Cala]], Barr [[Duel in the Royal Command Bunker|died]] having ensured [[Mon Calamari]] starships would [[Defense of the southern polar regions|rebel against the Empire]]. Barr had also recruited the Force-sensitive [[Verla]] as his apprentice,<ref name="Dark Lord 17" /> but, even though she survived the invasion, she would eventually give up on the Jedi path, choosing to go into hiding instead.<ref name="Star Wars 2020 6">[[Star Wars (2020) 6|''Star Wars'' (2020) 6]]</ref>

[[File:CalVsTrilla.png|thumb|250px|Though hunted by Inquisitors, Cal Kestis sought to restore the fallen order by training a new generation of Jedi.|left]]
In [[14 BBY]],<ref name="14 BBY Note">''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of ''[[Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order]]'' to [[14 BBY]].</ref> the Padawan [[Cal Kestis]], after being discovered by the Empire and escaping the Inquisitors at [[Bracca]], joined former Jedi Knight [[Cere Junda]] on a quest to restore the Jedi Order. Both searched for a [[Eno Cordova's holocron|holocron]] containing a list of Force-sensitive youth across the galaxy, which was hidden by Jedi Master [[Eno Cordova]]. Although they both obtained the holocron after a few clashes with the Inquisitors and one with Darth Vader, Kestis decided to destroy it to keep the young men on the list safe from the Empire.<ref name="JFO" />
[[File:TensuRunRegisKor-Inquisitors1.png|thumb|250x250px|Jedi Knight Tensu Run became a symbol of something the Empire could not tolerate: hope.]]
Jedi Knight [[Tensu Run]] became a threat to the Empire, as after freeing prisoners from an [[Imperial outpost (Regis Kor)|Imperial outpost]] during the [[Conquest of Regis Kor]], he became a symbol of hope. Tensu Run's [[death]] became one of the Inquisitorius' highest priorities, with [[the Grand Inquisitor]],<ref name="Inquisitors 1">[[Inquisitors 1|''Inquisitors'' 1]]</ref> the [[Fifth Brother]],<ref name="Inquisitors 2">[[Inquisitors 2|''Inquisitors'' 2]]</ref> the [[Seventh Sister]] and the [[Ninth Sister]],<ref name="Inquisitors 3">[[Inquisitors 3|''Inquisitors'' 3]]</ref> all participating in the [[Hunt for Tensu Run|hunt]]. The Inquisitors were defeated more than once by the Jedi Knight, who, along with other survivors of Order 66, sought to restore the Jedi Order. Due to the Inquisitors' failures, Darth Vader led the four Inquisitors in a final confrontation with the Jedi, which resulted in Run's death by the hands of the Sith Lord, as well as the other Jedi, who were killed by the Inquisitors.<ref name="Inquisitors 4">[[Inquisitors 4|''Inquisitors'' 4]]</ref>

[[File:CalKestisSecondLightsaberCrossguard-Survivor.jpg|thumb|250px|Cal Kestis became one of the most wanted Jedi by the Galactic Empire in 9 BBY.|left]]
Over the five years following the holocron's destruction, Kestis has become an extremely important target for the Empire, having attracted the attention of not only the Inquisitorius, but the [[Imperial Security Bureau|ISB]] as well.<ref name="Star Wars Jedi: Survivor">''[[Star Wars Jedi: Survivor]]''</ref> In [[9 BBY]],<ref name="Survivor Date">{{JediSurvivorDate}}</ref> on the planet [[Koboh]], Kestis encountered something from the Jedi's golden age. Kestis encountered the Jedi [[Dagan Gera]], who has been preserved in bacta since the days of the High Republic. Kestis freed the old Jedi and asked for his help in his fight against the Empire. However, Gera fell out with the Jedi Order, who he believed had betrayed him because the Jedi had given up on [[Tanalorr]], a hard-to-reach world Dagan had become obsessed with, after an [[Attack on Tanalorr|attack]] by the [[Nihil]]. Gera fell to the dark side and bled the kyber crystal from his lightsaber, starting a duel with Kestis afterwards. Dagan escaped with the help of his old ally, the [[Gen'Dai]] [[Rayvis]], and intended to return to Tanalorr and create an army led by Force users trained by himself to fight the Empire. However, due to the clouded view of Gera by the dark side, Kestis opposed his plan. Along with [[Bode Akuna]], Kestis killed Dagan and obtained the compass that would guide them to Tanalorr, a place that Kestis intended to transform into a refuge for those persecuted by the Empire.<ref name="Star Wars Jedi: Survivor" />

[[File:Dagan_Gera.png|thumb|330x330px|Dagan Gera, a High Republic-era Jedi who had been in suspended animation for centuries, was found and freed by Jedi Knight Cal Kestis.]]
However, the compass was stolen by Akuna, who was an ISB's spy and a survivor of the Jedi Purge. Akuna intended to flee to Tanalorr with his daughter so that they could live free from the Empire forever, which, in his opinion, Kestis' intentions for Tanalorr jeopardized. Kestis followed Akuna to Tanalorr, and along with his ally, the [[Nightsisters|Nightsister]] [[Merrin]], slew him. Kestis and his friends took in Bode's daughter and held a Jedi funeral for Akuna, Cere Junda, and Eno Cordova, who were trying to restore knowledge from the [[Jedi Archives]] and were killed due to Akuna stealing the compass. Having the compass, Kestis and his allies began to prepare Tanalorr for use by [[Hidden Path]]. Kestis also intended to use Tanalorr as a location to continue Cere's work of gathering knowledge from the Jedi Archives.<ref name="Star Wars Jedi: Survivor">''[[Star Wars Jedi: Survivor]]''</ref>

In [[5 BBY]],<ref name="Spark Date">{{RebelsDate|101}}</ref> one survivor, [[Kanan Jarrus]], formerly known as the Padawan Caleb Dume,<ref name="Kanan 1">[[Kanan 1|''Kanan'' 1]]</ref> took on a Padawan of his own, [[Ezra Bridger]]. Both of them worked as part of the [[Spectres]], a rebel crew based out of the [[VCX-100 light freighter]] ''[[Ghost]]'' that often struck at the Empire on [[Lothal]].<ref name="Spark">''[[Star Wars Rebels: Spark of Rebellion]]''</ref> During the [[action at Mustafar]], Jarrus and Bridger confronted [[the Grand Inquisitor]], who chose to take his own life instead of facing the wrath of his masters for failing to defeat them. The Spectres then joined up with the larger [[Phoenix Cell]], which let Jarrus and Bridger work with Ahsoka Tano, who had become a [[Fulcrum]] agent for [[Bail Organa's resistance movement]] and the overall growing rebellion. These rebel cells entered into a [[Galactic Civil War]] against the Empire.<ref name="Fire Across the Galaxy" />

[[File:218-AhsokavVader.png|thumb|300px|Vader confronted his former apprentice, the former Jedi Ahsoka Tano, in a Sith temple on Malachor.|left]]
Master [[Yoda]] had also survived the purge, having survived both Order 66 and a [[duel in the Galactic Senate]] against Sidious.<ref name="Episode III" /> He based himself on the remote planet of [[Dagobah]] to avoid Imperial hunters,<ref name="USW" /> though he was able to connect with the Lothal Jedi on two occasions through the [[World Between Worlds]].<ref name="POTJ">{{Rebels|Path of the Jedi}}</ref><ref name="Shroud of Darkness">{{Rebels|Shroud of Darkness}}</ref> On the second occasion, Tano learned Vader was in fact her former mentor Skywalker, Yoda told Bridger to go to Malachor when he asked for advice on fighting the Sith, and Jarrus was knighted by a vision of the Grand Inquisitor.<ref name="Shroud of Darkness" /> During the [[Mission to Malachor]], Tano finally encountered Vader. She again affirmed she was not a Jedi in order to seek revenge for her mentor's demise, as Skywalker had effectively died when he became Vader. At the end of their duel, Tano was presumed dead at Vader's hands,<ref name="Twilight of the Apprentice" /> but she had actually been saved by Bridger sometime later using the World Between Worlds.<ref name="AWBW">{{Rebels|A World Between Worlds}}</ref>

Before he reached the point in his life where he rescued Tano, Bridger and the other rebels lived through much.<ref name="AWBW" /> In [[2 BBY]],<ref name="Timelines" /><ref name="Twin Suns date">{{RebelsDate|320}}</ref> the Spectres and other rebel cells officially formed into the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]],<ref name="Secret Cargo">{{Rebels|Secret Cargo}}</ref> and the former Sith Lord Maul was [[Mission to Tatooine (Imperial Era)|struck down]] on Tatooine by his old nemesis, Obi-Wan Kenobi. Before dying in his enemy's arms, Maul asked if the individual Kenobi was guarding on the desert world was the Chosen One. Believing Luke Skywalker was, Kenobi said as such, giving Maul hope that they would be avenged.<ref name="Twin Suns">{{Rebels|Twin Suns (episode)}}</ref>

[[File:Ezra_before_being_sent_into_hyperspace.jpg|thumb|250px|The Jedi Ezra Bridger went missing after the liberation of his home planet of Lothal.]]
In [[1 BBY]],<ref name="Timelines" /> Jarrus's lover,<ref name="Jedi Night">{{Rebels|Jedi Night}}</ref> General [[Hera Syndulla]], was captured after a failed Rebel Alliance [[Attack on Lothal|assault]] on the heavily-occupied Lothal.<ref name="Rebel Assault">{{Rebels|Rebel Assault}}</ref> Jarrus was able to [[Rescue of Hera Syndulla (Lothal)|rescue]] her, but he soon had to give his life to protect Bridger, Syndulla, and the Mandalorian [[Sabine Wren]].<ref name="Jedi Night">{{Rebels|Jedi Night}}</ref> A short time later, Bridger entered the World Between Worlds and rescued Tano. While making sure Sidious would be unable to secure the power of the World Between Worlds, Tano and Bridger again parted ways, with Tano promising to find him when the time came.<ref name="AWBW" /> Bridger then led the [[Liberation of Lothal|effort to liberate]] his homeworld of Lothal. During the battle, Bridger spoke with [[Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo|Thrawn]], who stated the Jedi had been reduced to those who were beaten, hidden away, or inexpertly trained Padawans. After again denying Sidious entrance into the World Between Worlds and having had a pod of [[purrgil]] summoned to Lothal, Bridger used [[Taming beasts|beast control]] to have the creatures take him, Thrawn, and the Star Destroyer ''[[Chimaera]]'' away<ref name="Family&Farewell">{{Rebels|Family Reunion – and Farewell}}</ref> to deep space.<ref name="Ultimate Star Wars NE">''[[Ultimate Star Wars, New Edition]]''</ref> Though Bridger's disappearance took another Jedi out of galactic affairs, the purrgil had taken out the [[Seventh Fleet (Galactic Empire)|7th Fleet]], and the Padawan's effort against Thrawn had successfully liberated Lothal.<ref name="Family&Farewell" />

===Rebirth of the Jedi===
====Luke Skywalker joins the Rebellion====
{{Quote|The Jedi are extinct. Their fire has gone out of the universe. You, my friend, are all that's left of their religion.|Wilhuff Tarkin, to Darth Vader|<ref name="Episode IV" />}}
When it seemed as though the Jedi had been destroyed, the Imperial [[Inquisitor]]s vanished as well.<ref name="Secrets of the Jedi" /> [[Grand Moff]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin]], a member of the Empire's leading triumvirate along with Darth Vader and Emperor Palpatine,<ref name="Tarkin">[[Tarkin (novel)|''Tarkin'']]</ref> considered Vader the last remnant of the Jedi faith,<ref name="Episode IV" /> although four of the Rebellion's [[Alliance guiding principles|guiding principles]] were near-quotations of Jedi texts.<ref name="EA1">{{StoryCite|story=Epilogue|book=Empire Ascendant 1}}</ref> Additionally, [[Imperial officer]] [[Arvira]] of the [[logistics corps]] believed even saying the word "Jedi" in Imperial territory was unadvisable.<ref name="The Sith of Datawork">{{StoryCite|story=The Sith of Datawork|book=From a Certain Point of View}}</ref>
